# Plan: overnight SPE rounds for triage (r05 and after)

The situation does not give round 4's measured numbers. I took the "Same as last round" values below from `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` as my default. Before I save the r05 prediction, I will check them against that file. If any value differs, I will use the file's value and keep the same stated deltas.

## Overnight limits (defaults, since none were given)

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Round cap | 4 rounds, r05 to r08 |
| Spend cap per round | $35 |
| Spend cap for the night | $120 |
| Git | Local commits and tags only. No push. |
| Outbound | No replies go to customers. No ticketing system writes. No messages. |

Approving this plan approves r05 as written. It also lets me run r06 to r08 on my own using the same steps. Each later plan is saved to `spe/plans/rNN.md` with the author "Claude, autonomous default under r05 approval".

## Round 5: Specify

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R5-1 | Keep A, B, C, D unchanged as controls. | User: "Keep running SPE rounds" | Config file hashes match r04. |
| R5-2 | Add config E. E is D with A's 30-line prompt. This is the only difference. | r04 proposal (D lost P1 recall), adopted as default | `diff` of E against D shows only the prompt file. |
| R5-3 | Run 3 trials per ticket per config. | Default, to measure noise on 40 tickets | 40 x 5 x 3 = 600 trials, minus logged skips. |
| R5-4 | Report P1 recall as its own metric, with the count of P1 tickets. | Default. A missed P1 is a missed outage. | Grader output lists P1 ticket IDs. |
| R5-5 | Trial tools are stubs. No draft reply leaves the sandbox. | Guidance: never send in an unattended loop | Transcript scan finds 0 calls to live endpoints. |
| R5-6 | Unattended rounds do not hand-tune prompt wording against the 40 tickets. | Default, to avoid overfitting the only eval set | Only the named config change appears in the diff. |
| R5-7 | Stay under $35 for the round. Skip and log trials that would cross it. | Default overnight cap | Cost meter total in results. |

Rejected proposal: "Add 20 harder tickets." Only the support lead can supply reference labels for new tickets. I logged this in `spe/spec/disagreements.md` as an open decision with the user as owner.

Defaults chosen tonight go into `spe/spec/disagreements.md` under "Logged defaults".

## Round 5: Predict

Naive guess means "same as last round". Each band is plus or minus the stated amount. A hit means the measured value is inside the band.

| Metric (grader check) | A | B | C | D | E | Band | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy (`check_category_exact`) | 0.90 | 0.90 | 0.88 | 0.83 | 0.86 | ± 0.05 | A to D unchanged. E gets the longer category rubric, so it moves part way from D toward C. |
| Priority exact (`check_priority_exact`) | 0.75 | 0.73 | 0.73 | 0.65 | 0.69 | ± 0.06 | A to D unchanged. The 30-line prompt holds the priority rules that B dropped, so E gains on D. |
| P1 recall, 6 tickets (`check_p1_recall`) | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.83 | 0.67 | 0.83 | ± 0.17 | One ticket equals 0.17. E's prompt names outage signals, so E catches one more P1 than D. |
| Reply pass rate (`judge_reply_rubric`) | 0.85 | 0.83 | 0.83 | 0.75 | 0.79 | ± 0.06 | A to D unchanged. E gains on tone rules but stays below Sonnet. |
| Schema valid (`check_schema`) | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.98 | 0.98 | ± 0.02 | No schema change. E inherits D's rate. |
| Cost per ticket in USD (`meter_cost`) | 0.040 | 0.034 | 0.030 | 0.010 | 0.013 | ± 0.004 | E adds about 18 prompt lines of input to D. |

`same_as_last_round: true` for every A to D cell. E has no prior round, so its naive guess is D's r04 value.

## Round 5: Evaluate

Gates. Each must pass before launch. If one fails, I halt and report.

1. Grader selftest. The oracle answers pass. Empty and wrong answers fail.
2. Control regrade of r04. Code checks must reproduce r04 exactly. The judge must land within 0.02 of r04.
3. Dry run on 2 cells, A and E, with 3 tickets each.

Workflow arguments:

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| `ROUND` | 5 (one constant, not typed into prompt text) |
| `configs` | A, B, C, D, E |
| `tickets` | the existing 40-ticket set |
| `trials_per_cell` | 3 |
| `extra_trials_on_split` | up to 2 more per split ticket, 60 extra at most |
| `spend_cap_usd` | 35 |

Harness rules: trials get a schema. Code checks run first. The judge scores only reply quality. Trials cannot read graders, reference labels, or predictions. A transcript scan voids any trial that peeked. The run ends with failure analysis and a completeness critic.

Cost estimate (unmeasured): about $15 for 360 Sonnet trials, about $3 for 240 Haiku trials, about $6 for 600 judge calls, and about $2 for extra trials. That totals about $26.

## Steps and local commits per round

1. Save the plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Save `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` with the "Saved before the eval ran" header. Commit `SPE r05 specify` and `SPE r05 predict: E = D + 30-line prompt`.
2. Write `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` and run the gates. Commit `SPE r05 evaluate (harness)`.
3. Launch the Workflow. Wait for its completion notice.
4. Commit `SPE r05 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
5. Learn. Update `spe/prediction-log.md` with the Which Why broke section and the naive comparison. Add new F entries to `spe/failures.md` after reading the highest F number. Add "Proposed for round 6" to the spec. Write `spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml` marked `status: draft`. Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r05 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r05`.

## Rounds 6 to 8

Each round starts from the previous round's proposals and measured values. I adopt or reject each proposal and record the reason as a logged default. Each new config changes one thing. A to D stay as controls unless a round shows one adds nothing. In that case I drop it and log why. The same gates, caps, and commit steps apply.

## Stop and halt

I stop early when predictions hit for 3 rounds in a row. If r04 was a hit, it counts toward the 3.

I halt and report when any of these happens:

- A spend cap would be crossed.
- A gate fails or a grader bug appears.
- A trial reads an answer key.
- Every config passes everything. Harder tickets need the support lead's labels, so this is your decision.

## Morning report

The report goes in chat and in `spe/README.md`. It gives each round's headline, a table of hits and misses per round compared with the naive guess, total spend, and the open decisions from `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. All work stays in local commits for you to review.
